facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus was named and described in 2009 by Clifford Miles and Clark Miles.
facts.quote: It was named and described in 2009 by Clifford Miles and Clark Miles.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Minotaurasaurus has been suspected to have been illegally exported from Mongolia.
facts.quote: The holotype of Minotaurasaurus has been suspected to be illegally exported out of Mongolia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Minotaurasaurus is a distinct genus or a synonym of Tarchia.
facts.quote: It has been suggested to be a synonym of Tarchia but more recent publications consider it as a distinct genus.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus likely had a tail club used for defense and was covered in protective osteoderms.
facts.quote: Although not a lot of postcranial material is known, it would have had a tail club that may have been used for protection against predators or interspecific combat and would have been covered in protective osteoderms.

facts.statement: The type specimen skull was purchased in 2003 for $10,000 by neuroscientist Vilayanur S. Ramachandran at a showcase in Arizona.
facts.quote: In 2003, a skull of an ankylosaurid was purchased for US$10,000 by the private fossil collector and neuroscientist Vilayanur S. Ramachandran while accompanied by Clifford Miles at the Tucson Gem, Mineral and Fossil Showcase, Arizona.

facts.statement: The skull was formally described and named in 2009.
facts.quote: The skull would later be described and named in 2009.

facts.statement: A second specimen was discovered in 2013 at the Uhkaa Tolgod locality in the Djadochta Formation.
facts.quote: In 2013, a Society of Vertebrate Paleontology abstract book mentioned the discovery of a second specimen of Minotaurasaurus (MAE 98 179) from the Uhkaa Tolgod locality of the late Campanian Djadochta Formation in the Nemegt Basin.

facts.statement: A second specimen shows insect burrows in a pattern unique to Late Cretaceous Gobi deposits.
facts.quote: MAE 98 179 was reported as having insect burrows that continues into a pattern which is only seen in Late Cretaceous Gobi deposits.

facts.statement: The original description faced criticism from paleontologists regarding the questionable legal origins of the specimen.
facts.quote: The publication was later criticised by palaeontologists such as Mark Norell, Phillip J. Currie and Bolortsetseg Minjin due to the questionable origins of the specimen.

facts.statement: The initial estimate of 4.2 meters (13.8 feet) likely underestimates the adult size because the known specimen is immature.
facts.quote: Miles & Miles (2009) gave Minotaurasaurus an estimated length of at least 4.2 metres (13.8 feet), although it may have attained larger sizes as the type specimen, and only known specimen at the time, represents an immature individual based on the unfused osteoderms.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus possessed an unfused occiput on its skull roof.
facts.quote: The skull roof possessing an unfused occiput.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus had highly sculptured squamosal horns that were narrow and cylindrical.
facts.quote: Highly sculptured squamosal horns that are dorsoventrally narrow and cylindrical in shape.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus had two distinct supraorbital apices.
facts.quote: The presence of two distinct supraorbital apices.

facts.statement: The frontal caputegulae were not arranged at right angles, while the nasofrontal ones were elongated transversely and ridge-like.
facts.quote: Frontal caputegulae that aren't arranged at right angles but with nasofrontal caputegulae that are elongated transversely and are ridge-like.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus had two pairs of internarial osteoderms, distinguishing it from Tarchia and Saichania which have only one.
facts.quote: The presence of two pairs of internarial osteoderms, unlike the presence of a single osteoderm as in Tarchia and Saichania.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus had a more horizontal pterygoid body.
facts.quote: A more horizontal pterygoid body.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Minotaurasaurus is 30 centimetres long and 43 centimetres wide.
facts.quote: The holotype skull measures 30 centimetres (11.8 inches) long and has a width of 43 centimetres (17 inches).

facts.statement: The squamosal horns of Minotaurasaurus are more slender and tapering than those of other ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike other ankylosaurids, the squamosal horns are more gracile and tapering.

facts.statement: Pyramid-shaped caputegulae cover most of the skull roof except for the area near the orbits.
facts.quote: Pyramid-shaped caputegulae cover most of the surface of the skull, with the exception of an area of the skull roof that is near the orbits.

facts.statement: All teeth of Minotaurasaurus are leaf-shaped.
facts.quote: All teeth are leaf-shaped.

facts.statement: The left maxilla contains 17 teeth and alveoli, while the right maxilla contains 16.
facts.quote: There are a total of 17 teeth and alveoli in the left maxilla and 16 in the right maxilla.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus was a herbivorous bulk feeder with a broad, sub-rectangular muzzle.
facts.quote: Minotaurasaurus was, like other Mongolian ankylosaurines, herbivorous and a low-level bulk feeder based on its sub-rectangular broad muzzle.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Minotaurasaurus may have relied on hindgut fermentation or eaten succulent plants rather than complex chewing due to its dry environment.
facts.quote: Instead of oral processing, ankylosaurids living in dry environments such as Minotaurasaurus may have relied more on hindgut fermentation for digestion or, alternatively, consumed succulent plants that did not require complex chewing.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus lived in an arid environment with sand dunes and short-lived water bodies during a warm, semiarid climate.
facts.quote: Based on the strata, rock facies, sedimentation and coeval units, the Djadochta Formation represents an arid environment consisting of sand dunes and short-lived water bodies with a warm, semiarid climate.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus lived during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Magnetostratigraphic datings from the Bayn Dzak and Tugriken Shireh localities suggest that the formation dates to the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, ca. ~75-71 Ma.

facts.statement: The remains of Minotaurasaurus were recovered from the Ukhaa Tolgod locality in the Djadochta Formation.
facts.quote: The remains of Minotaurasaurus were likely recovered from the Ukhaa Tolgod locality at the Djadochta Formation.

facts.statement: The genus Minotaurasaurus was named by Miles & Miles in 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Miles & Miles, 2009

facts.statement: The species Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani was named by Miles & Miles in 2009.
facts.quote: species_authority: Miles & Miles, 2009

facts.statement: Arbour et al. (2014) and Arbour & Currie (2015) considered Minotaurasaurus a junior synonym of Tarchia kielanae based on a shared furrow near the squamosal horn.
facts.quote: Arbour et al. (2014) considered Minotaurasaurus as a junior synonym of Tarchia kielanae due to the shared presence of a furrow near the squamosal horn, a conclusion also met by Arbour & Currie (2015).

facts.statement: Penkalski & Tumanova (2016) argued that Minotaurasaurus is a valid taxon distinct from Tarchia due to differences in squamosal horns and caputegulae.
facts.quote: However, Penkalski & Tumanova (2016) noted that it differs from Tarchia by a number of characteristics, such as differences in the squamosal horns and caputegulae, and stated that it should therefore be considered as a valid taxon.

facts.statement: Thomas et al. (2012) and Han et al. (2014) recovered Minotaurasaurus as the sister taxon to Pinacosaurus grangeri in phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Thomas et al. (2012) recovered it as sister taxon to Pinacosaurus grangeri, a position also recovered by Han et al. (2014).

facts.statement: Penkalski & Tumanova (2016) found Minotaurasaurus at the base of a clade containing Zaraapelta, Saichania, and Tarchia.
facts.quote: Penkalski & Tumanova (2016) also conducted a phylogenetic analysis which found Minotaurasaurus as being at the base of a clade containing Zaraapelta, Saichania and Tarchia.

facts.statement: Wiersma & Irmis (2018) recovered Minotaurasaurus within a polytomy with Tarchia kielanae and Shanxia.
facts.quote: Wiersma & Irmis (2018) recovered it within a polytomy with Tarchia kielanae and Shanxia.

facts.statement: Park et al. (2021) suggested a shift from bulk to selective feeding in Mongolian ankylosaurines was caused by climate change or competition with hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Park et al. (2021) suggested that there was a shift from bulk feeding to selective feeding in Mongolian ankylosaurines during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages which may have either been caused by the change in habitat, as the climate changed from semi-arid and arid to humid, or interspecific competition with saurolophine hadrosaurids that immigrated from North America to Central Asia during the Campanian stage.

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani is the only known species of the extinct genus Minotaurasaurus, a thyreophoran ankylosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani es la única especie conocida del género extinto Minotaurasaurus (gr. "lagarto minotauro") de dinosaurio tireóforo anquilosáurido

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 to 70 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 75 a 70 millones de años, durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Minotaurasaurus were found in the Gobi Desert, though it is not specified whether the location is in China or Mongolia.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se encontraron en el desierto de Gobi, pero no se precisa si es en China o en Mongolia

facts.statement: The skull of Minotaurasaurus is triangular in dorsal view and features large, ornate nasal osteoderms that give it a bull-like appearance with laterally open nostril windows.
facts.quote: Tiene forma de triángulo equilátero en vista dorsal y osteodermos nasales grandes, muy adornados, que le dan un aspecto de toro con las ventanas de la nariz abiertas lateralmente

facts.statement: The type specimen of Minotaurasaurus is a virtually complete and intact skull including both jaw rami and the complete predentary bone.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo es un cráneo virtualmente completo e intacto con ambas ramas de la mandíbulas y el predentario completo

facts.statement: The genus name Minotaurasaurus means 'minotaur lizard' in Greek, referring to the bull-like appearance of the skull similar to the Minotaur of Greek mythology.
facts.quote: El nombre del género que significa lagarto hombre-toro proviene del griego, en referencia al aspecto de toro del cráneo, similar al Minotauro de la mitología griega

facts.statement: The specific name ramachandrani honors V.S. Ramachandran, who ensured the skull was described and made it available to science.
facts.quote: El nombre específico está puesto en honor a V.S. Ramachandran, que se cercioró de que este cráneo fuera descrito y lo puso a disposición de la ciencia

facts.statement: The skull was purchased by V.S. Ramachandran and was originally exhibited at the Victor Valley Museum in California, USA.
facts.quote: El cráneo fue comprado por V.S. Ramachandran y exhibido originalmente en el Museo del Valle Victor, California, EE. UU

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani exhibits typical characteristics of many Upper Cretaceous ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani muestra los caracteres típicos de muchos anquilosáuridos del Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: The characteristics of the cranial box of Minotaurasaurus are more primitive than those of other ankylosaurids from the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: Las características de la caja craneana son más primitivas que las de los otros anquilosáuridos del desierto de Gobi

facts.statement: A 2014 study by Victoria Arbour, Philip Currie, and Demchig Badamgarav concluded that Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani is actually a junior synonym of Tarchia kielanae.
facts.quote: Un estudio publicado en 2014 de Victoria Arbour, Philip Currie y Demchig Badamgarav concluyó que Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani es en realidad un sinónimo más moderno de Tarchia kielanae

facts.statement: However, a 2016 redescription of Tarchia cranial anatomy concluded that Minotaurasaurus is a distinct taxon.
facts.quote: sin embargo. una redescripción de la anatomía craneana de Tarchia publicada en 2016, concluyó que Minotaurasaurus era un taxón distinto

facts.statement: The parent group of Minotaurasaurus is Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus belongs to the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Minotaurasaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
